newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: TULIP SAYS SEES NET LOSS OVER FULL 1996.
newsitem.headline: TULIP SAYS SEES NET LOSS OVER FULL 1996.

text.p: Personal computer maker Tulip said on Tuesday it expected to post a loss over the full 1996 year.
"In line with expectations...management expects to close the second half of 1996 in profit. However the profit will not be sufficient to end the full year in profit," Tulip said in a statement.

In August the company said it expected to return to profit in the second half of 1996 after a first-half net loss of 12.7 million guilders, but added it did not know whether to expect a profit or loss for the whole year.
Tulip said that preliminary talks on a strategic partnership, announced earlier this year, had ended without result.
"The management of Tulip Computers says that no agreement has been reached on the details and conditions of this possible alliance. The talks have since been ended."
Speculation that the Dutch PC maker was in talks on a possible alliance with a large electronics manufacturer sent Tulip's shares surging on the Amsterdam Stock Exchange.
